reading.body:
Data engineering roles dominate AI hiring across tracked sources, with eight open positions spanning autonomous vehicles, cybersecurity, and enterprise platforms from September 2026.

The concentration of data engineering postings reflects a structural reality: models require pipelines before they require researchers. Every AI system needs someone to build the infrastructure that moves, validates, and prepares data at scale. The geographic spread—from Arlington County to Prague to Mountain View—shows this work is not centralized. Remote work appears in at least one role, though most postings specify physical locations, suggesting data infrastructure work often requires presence near compute resources or regional teams.

Salary data is sparse. One disclosed figure reaches $123,122 annually for an AI and data engineering support role, but the dataset does not provide enough salary information to establish trends or regional variation. Most postings list job titles without compensation, limiting visibility into market rates for this function.

The data does not capture hiring volume trends, unfilled positions, or competition for roles. It does not distinguish between roles building training infrastructure versus production data systems, a meaningful difference in downstream compute demands. It reflects openings posted to public boards and company career pages as of mid-September 2026, and thus omits roles filled through recruiting firms or not yet publicized.
